text:
Pittsburgh · Cultural District

About the Arcade

Pittsburgh's home for live comedy since 2013.

Arcade Comedy Theater is a 501(c)(3) non-profit theater in the heart of Pittsburgh's Cultural District that produces, presents, and educates in the art of comedy. The Arcade was founded in 2013 as the city's first non-profit theater exclusively dedicated to comedy, with a mission to strengthen and enrich the community through laughter for all. In 2017, the theater expanded from a small storefront to a custom, accessible three-story, two-theater facility to serve more artists and audiences.

The theater presents programming 52 weekends a year in improv, stand-up, sketch, and other comedic forms, plus a bi-monthly matinee improv show for kids. Classes for all ages and levels are taught by professional actors and comedians within the Arcade Academy, and Arcade's Corporate Training strengthens the communication skills of professionals throughout Southwestern Pennsylvania. Arcade has been named "Best Place to See Live Comedy" by the readers of Pittsburgh Magazine multiple times, and has been featured in WQED, Yahoo News, and Paste Magazine.

Mission & Vision

Our mission

Arcade Comedy Theater inspires joy and nurtures community-building by connecting artists and audiences with the dynamic artform of comedy. With exceptional performances and educational offerings, Arcade entertains and uplifts Pittsburgh audiences and beyond.

Our vision

Arcade will elevate and advance the art of comedy, by fostering a safe, inclusive space to explore and play with humor. In doing so, our community finds artistic fulfillment, confidence, and healing through the development of their unique comedic voice. Our audiences experience exciting, engaging, and spirit-lifting performances that showcase comedy in its many forms.

Our Values

Inclusivity & Safety

Comedy must reflect the diverse world in which it is presented. Humor can hurt as easily as it can help, and a foundation of trust is necessary to enjoy the artform. Arcade will ensure equitable practices and swiftly remedy when our foundation is cracked.

Affordability

Arcade is proud to be positioned as the most affordable live entertainment offering in downtown Pittsburgh's Cultural District. Laughter and levity should be experienced by all. Through programs like our kids' show "Pay As You Wish," Academy internships, and the Diversity Scholarship, we strive to break down barriers to entry.

Variety

Like our namesake, Arcade was founded with a vision to showcase many different styles within one form of live entertainment. We broaden the audience's preconceived notion of "comedy" by producing everything from proven standards to offbeat styles.

Experimentation

Improv and other forms of comedic expression depend on artists feeling free to try new things, fail, and try again. Arcade's Academy encourages students to "play" and teammates to support one another's new ideas made up on the spot. Honing a unique comedic voice takes a willingness to experiment with an open mind.

Collaboration

Arcade values the wisdom, creativity, and input of our community — a vibrant group of artists, audiences, designers, technicians, students, staff, and volunteers. We forge partnerships with our downtown neighbors, the city's non-profit arts organizations, and comedy organizations across the world.

Arcade is led by a dedicated staff and a volunteer Board of Directors committed to charity, fiscal discipline, and inclusion.

Arcade Comedy Theater Names Kathryn Spitz Cohan Executive Director

New leader will help shape the next chapter for Pittsburgh's home for comedy

PITTSBURGH, PA (October 7, 2026)
– Arcade Comedy Theater has named Kathryn Spitz Cohan its new Executive Director. Kathryn will lead the business of making comedy possible: strengthening business operations, administration, fundraising, and organizational development while partnering with Arcade’s programming, education, and production leaders and Board of Directors.

Kathryn brings more than two decades of experience in nonprofit leadership and arts administration. She is the founder and was the former Executive Director of Film Pittsburgh, where from 2001–2025 she oversaw programs including the Three Rivers Film Festival, Pittsburgh Shorts and Script Competition, JFilm Festival, ReelAbilities Pittsburgh, Teen Screen, and the Robinson Short Film Competition.

“I was drawn to Arcade because of its commitment to artists, its sense of community, and the people who make it happen. Everyone involved has a love for the theater that is infectious,” said Kathryn. “I’m excited to get to know and work with the Arcade team, learn from this community, and help support the people and creative work that make Arcade such a distinctive part of Pittsburgh’s arts community.”

Kathryn’s first priorities will include listening to performers, students, staff, volunteers, audiences, and other stakeholders; understanding what is working well and where Arcade can strengthen its foundation; and supporting the creative work and community at the heart of the organization, all in service of giving Arcade’s artists, students, and audiences even more reasons to show up and laugh together.

Arcade Comedy Theater is a 501(c)(3) nonprofit in downtown Pittsburgh dedicated to presenting fun, accessible, and affordable live comedy. Through performances, classes, and community engagement, Arcade provides an inclusive space where artists and audiences connect, create, and celebrate the art of laughter.

Arcade Comedy Theater is a 501(c)3 non-profit theater organization located in the heart of Pittsburgh's Cultural District that produces, presents, and educates in the art of comedy. The Arcade was founded in 2013 as the city's first non-profit theater exclusively dedicated to comedy, with a mission to strengthen and enrich the community through laughter for all. In 2017, the theater successfully expanded from a small storefront to a custom and accessible three-story, two-theater facility in order to serve more artists and audiences with new programming and class opportunities.

The theater presents a variety of programming 52 weekends a year in improv, stand-up, sketch, and other comedic forms, plus a bi-monthly matinee improv show for kids. Improv, sketch, and stand-up comedy classes for all ages and levels are taught by talented professional actors and comedians within the Arcade Academy. Arcade's Corporate Training and Entertainment strengthens the communication skills of professionals and makes work fun throughout Southwestern Pennsylvania. Arcade has been named "Best Place to See Live Comedy" by the readers of Pittsburgh Magazine multiple times, and has been featured in WQED, Yahoo News, and Paste Magazine. Learn more at arcadecomedytheater.com.
